blocks.content: National income is a key macroeconomic concept used to measure the economic performance of a country. It represents the total monetary value of all final goods and services produced in a nation during a specific period, usually one year.
1. Meaning of National Income

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: National Income represents the total net value of all final goods and services produced by a country's residents within a financial year.
Net National Product (NNP) calculated at Factor Cost is officially defined as the National Income of a nation.
The three standard methods for estimating National Income are the Production (Value Added) Method, Income Method, and Expenditure Method.
In India, official National Income statistics are compiled and released by the National Statistical Office (NSO) under MoSPI.
Depreciation (Capital Consumption Allowance) is subtracted from Gross aggregates to derive Net aggregates.

blocks.content: • National income refers to the total value of all final goods and services produced in a country during a year.
• It measures the overall economic activity of a nation.
• It helps governments formulate economic policies and development plans.
• It is an indicator of economic growth and standard of living.
2. Important Concepts of National Income

cells: Total value of goods and services produced within the country's borders.
GDP plus income earned by citizens abroad minus income earned by foreigners.
GNP minus depreciation (wear and tear of capital).
Average income per person (National income divided by population).

blocks.content: 3. GDP Explained
• GDP measures the total production of goods and services within a country.
• It includes production by both domestic and foreign companies within the country.
• It is widely used as an indicator of economic performance.
• GDP can be calculated at market price or factor cost.
4. GNP Explained
• GNP measures the total income earned by residents of a country.
• It includes income from abroad earned by citizens.
Net National Product at Factor Cost is considered the true measure of National Income of a nation.
• It excludes income generated by foreign residents within the country.
5. NNP Explained
• NNP is obtained by subtracting depreciation from GNP.
• Depreciation refers to the wear and tear of machinery and equipment.
• NNP gives a more accurate measure of economic output.
6. Methods of Calculating National Income

cells: Adds the value of goods and services produced in different sectors.
Adds incomes earned by factors of production such as wages, rent, interest and profit.
Adds all expenditures on final goods and services in the economy.

blocks.content: 7. Components of National Income
• Wages – payments made to labour.

rows: Total market value of final goods & services produced within domestic territory.
Total market value of final goods & services produced by normal residents of a country worldwide.
GNP = GDP + Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA)
Includes income generated by foreign nationals within domestic territory.
Excludes income generated by foreign nationals within domestic territory; includes residents' foreign earnings.

blocks.content: • Rent – income received for use of land or property.
• Interest – income earned on capital.
• Profit – earnings of entrepreneurs.
8. Importance of National Income
• Measures economic growth and development.
• Helps government plan economic policies.
• Helps compare economic performance between countries.
• Indicates the standard of living of people.
9. Limitations of National Income
• Does not include unpaid household services.
• Does not reflect income inequality.

items: Transfer payments (like old-age pensions, scholarships, and unemployment benefits) are EXCLUDED from National Income calculation because no productive activity occurs.
Windfall gains (e.g., lotteries, gambling) and sale of second-hand goods are NOT included in National Income.
GDP measures production within domestic boundaries regardless of nationality, whereas GNP incorporates Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA).
Real GDP is measured at constant base-year prices to adjust for inflation, whereas Nominal GDP is measured at current market prices.

blocks.content: • Does not measure environmental damage.
• Does not show distribution of wealth.
10. National Income Estimation in India
In India, national income is estimated by the National Statistical Office (NSO) under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.
Important Facts
• GDP is the most widely used indicator of economic growth.
• Per capita income indicates the average income of citizens.
• In India, NSO estimates national income.
